brief.instructions: Generate at most two DIFFERENT practical improvements: (1) engine/rank-aware prefix reuse with bounded load-skew and load-only fallback, accounting for API2 and internal DP4; (2) adaptive prefill admission budget protecting decode deadlines with bounded TTFT and starvation. Strongest static comparator mandatory. Known existing techniques welcome; scientific novelty irrelevant. Do not propose flags already verified present. Presence not established: use first inspection gate. Distinguish cacheability target from observed cache hit. Source grounded useful proposals, no speedup claim. Test cheap causal falsification first. Proposed numeric thresholds are design choices not observations. No GPU execution now. Use held-out skew/prefix distributions and length-aware scorer.

target.workload: agent-f75 8192 input /1024 output, 75% cacheability target; Mooncake median/burst/cache-heavy replay

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Attribute missed decode deadlines in traces to prefill-bearing iterations, preemption events, and queueing before implementing the controller.
alternatives.explanation: Decode delays may mainly reflect KV pressure, preemption, or another source rather than prefill admission.

alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare against the best static budget and eligible fixed cadence chosen on a calibration split, then evaluate on held-out load regimes.
alternatives.explanation: A single well-tuned static token budget or cadence may already achieve the same tradeoff.

card.code_surface: V1 scheduler prefill admission, per-iteration timing telemetry, decode deadline estimate, per-request wait accounting.

reduced average end-to-end latency by 8.5% relative to fixed MBT 2k

experiment.control: LAT-2XDEP4-R7b as actually running, plus the strongest static max_num_batched_tokens or eligible fixed cadence selected on a calibration split under the same scorer.
experiment.correctness: Confirm each admitted request progresses within the wait bound and generated outputs remain unchanged; measure whole-trace inter-token gaps separately from per-request TPOT.
experiment.cost: First inspect scheduler configuration and analyze existing traces without GPU execution; later conduct one-factor replay and a bounded static-policy sweep.
experiment.held_out_condition: Mooncake median and burst traces plus unseen prompt and output-length mixes, including low-pressure periods and sustained prefill queues.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Runtime policy presence is unknown, timing traces cannot separate interference from preemption, or the held-out replay lacks mixed prefill-decode pressure.
experiment.metrics: Frozen length-aware SLO goodput; cost per successful request; E2E and TTFT p95; ITL p95 by output-length cohort; completed throughput; decode deadline misses; prefill wait tail and starvation count.
experiment.rejects_if: The cheap trace check finds no association between prefill admission and deadline misses, or the strongest static control matches or exceeds goodput, or TTFT and waiting bounds fail.
experiment.supports_if: Held-out mixed-load replay shows fewer decode deadline misses and better frozen SLO goodput than both controls while respecting the predeclared TTFT and waiting bounds.
experiment.treatment: Deadline-aware adaptive prefill admission with a predeclared maximum wait bound; routing and other factors held fixed.

card.mechanism: Limit admitted prefill work during decode pressure to reduce long mixed iterations, while releasing the cap when pressure falls or a prefill wait bound is reached.

novelty.implementation: The possible delta is a deadline and wait-bounded admission policy in the verified R7b scheduler, if absent.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: P-PAS RFC and paper propose pressure-adaptive prefill budgets; the deadline-aware chunking paper and decode-priority cadence PR identify related tradeoffs.
novelty.scientific: No novelty claim; adaptive prefill budgets and deadline-aware chunking are prior work.
novelty.specific_delta: Tie prefill admission to observed decode deadline slack and an explicit per-request waiting bound, then compare with the strongest static setting.
novelty.workload: Long-input agent-f75 and Mooncake mixed-load replay; actual decode interference and B200 effect are unknown.

card.observed_bottleneck: Unknown. The R7b baseline gives throughput and E2E p95, but no measured prefill interference, decode deadline misses, TTFT, or starvation.
card.predicted_direction: Conditional reduction in decode ITL deadline misses and higher SLO goodput, while TTFT and starvation remain within chosen bounds; no numerical gain predicted.
card.proposed_change: After the presence gate, add an optional V1 scheduler admission budget using current decode deadline slack and prefill pressure, with a maximum wait bound and fixed-budget fallback. Test this factor independently of routing.
card.statement: First inspect the effective scheduler commit and runtime settings to establish whether adaptive prefill admission already exists. If absent, test a scheduler-local prefill budget that decreases when active decodes approach their measured iteration deadlines and increases when decode pressure eases. Keep the global token budget fixed; bound each prefill request’s waiting time so decode protection cannot starve TTFT. This transfers the pressure-dependent budget mechanism described by P-PAS, while adding an explicit deadline and waiting bound for the R7b objective. The source reports results on other model and GPU configurations, so neither a B200 crossover nor an effect size is known. A cheap trace analysis should first test whether prefill-bearing iterations coincide with decode deadline misses before any GPU replay.

policy.baseline_comparison: Compare each change separately with LAT-2XDEP4-R7b and the strongest tuned static policy on the same held-out skew, prefix, and request-length distributions. The task reports closed-loop c384 throughput of 27.69 req/s with E2E p95 of 18.30s, and c512 throughput of 33.76 req/s with E2E p95 of 19.49s. The stated engine profile is desired state, not verified runtime state. Freeze the length-aware scorer and output-length cohorts before comparing SLO goodput, cost per successful request, latency, and completed throughput.

criteria.description: Required veto: show a credible, testable path to task value and either a delta from the verified baseline or a cheap inspection gate that determines whether the capability is already present. Unknown presence defers judgment.
criteria.justification: The router policy, rank targeting, effective commit, and adaptive prefill feature are unverified. Checking those first prevents proposing an already active flag while allowing useful experiments before a speedup is measured.

criteria.description: Specify the cheapest falsification test first, then a one-factor-at-a-time replay against the strongest tuned static comparator.
criteria.justification: Cacheability is a target, not an observed cache hit. Replay must measure rank-local hits, load skew, decode deadline misses, TTFT, starvation, and the frozen length-aware goodput score.

criteria.description: Show a plausible integration at API2 and the internal DP4 rank, with bounded load skew or admission delay and a specified fallback.
criteria.justification: Replica-only affinity cannot establish rank-local reuse. Admission control must protect decode without allowing unbounded prefill waiting.

criteria.description: Ground mechanism and baseline claims in the supplied evidence; label unknown implementation, hardware, workload, effect size, and limitations.
criteria.justification: The supplied PR and issue titles identify relevant work but provide no code, measurements, or implementation detail. The paper entries provide links and titles only.

evidence.rationale: One relevant engineering source suffices for an implementation claim; two sources or a paper are not automatic requirements. Here the available metadata cannot verify implementation or effects. Positive claims about existing behavior therefore await the first code and runtime inspection gate. Hypotheses and proposed tests may proceed with unknowns recorded.

policy.objective: Prioritize up to two practical improvements for the stated 8 B200 target: rank-aware prefix reuse with bounded load skew and load-only fallback, and adaptive prefill admission that protects decode deadlines while bounding TTFT and starvation.
policy.rationale: The 70-point threshold is an uncalibrated prioritization choice, not a measured success cutoff. Only the required improvement criterion is a veto; unknown judgments defer selection. Observed result: the task supplies the baseline figures quoted above, without independently verifiable run details. Author claims: titles such as “Add prefix-cache-aware routing for internal DP load balancing” and “Adaptive prefill token budget based on scheduling pressure” indicate relevant ideas, not verified behavior. Transfer inference: both ideas could plausibly address the stated workload, but their cache-hit rate, bottlenecks, effect size, tested hardware, workload match, and limitations remain unknown. Published status and scientific novelty have no selection role.

retrieval.rationale: This response uses only supplied material, as requested. A later authorized inspection should check the router, rank targeting, runtime configuration, and adaptive prefill presence before proposing implementation changes.

causal_test.rationale: The cheapest check asks whether prefill-bearing iterations coincide with decode deadline misses and separates preemption as an alternative. Association alone would not establish cause; the proposed one-factor held-out replay against R7b and tuned static controls provides the causal comparison. It includes TTFT, waiting, starvation, and output-length cohort metrics.

claim_discipline.rationale: The RFC’s “reduced average end-to-end latency by 8.5%” is presented as an author report from other configurations, with no B200 speedup prediction. The supplied paper says the effect “depends on the model–hardware configuration,” and another flags that “starvation and admission control deserve separate study.” Neither passage verifies this deployment’s implementation.

integration_and_bounds.rationale: Scheduler-local admission, a fixed global token budget, a maximum wait, and fixed-budget fallback are plausible. The RFC author states, “The global scheduler token budget remains unchanged.” The actual V1 scheduler path is unverified, and the proposal must define how forced prefill progress interacts with a simultaneous decode deadline before its bounds are assessable.

required_improvement.rationale: The scheduler inspection gate and trace question give a credible testable path. Whether an adaptive admission policy is absent, or prefill interferes with decode on this deployment, remains unknown. The supplied E2E results do not settle either question.

objections: Adaptive feature presence, decode deadline misses, TTFT, starvation, and B200 effect size are unknown.
A trace association is only a falsification screen; preemption and KV pressure remain alternative causes.
The static comparator should be chosen under the same frozen scorer and stated eligibility rules; the wait bound and fallback priority need precise definitions.

detailed_design.statistics: Paired identical arrival/prompt seeds; randomize treatment order; 3repeats forscreening,5repeats only finalists. Use trace-block bootstrap95%CI on paired primary deltas, and latency quantiles with requestcounts. Keep timeout requests in denominators. No adaptive choosing winning seeds.
detailed_design.stop: Stop immediately on output correctness regression, OOM/repeated errors, unbounded queue growth, or p99TTFT>2x pairedbaseline for>60s. A crash is executionerror, not invalidation.
